rounds.name: Worker-Kerr
rounds.text:
Withholding pay incentivizes the worker to do the job properly, yielding the highest possible payoff (5 tasks) and still gives a positive outcome even if they cut corners (1 task). Since it dominates trust in every scenario, I will withhold.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Ellis
rounds.text:
Withholding pay always yields at least 1 completed task and up to 5 if the worker does the job properly, which dominates the outcomes from trusting (3 or 0). Since we want to maximize expected completed tasks regardless of the worker’s choice, the safe strategy is to withhold.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Jarvis
rounds.text:
Withholding pay always yields at least as many completed tasks as trusting, because even if the worker does the job properly you get 5 tasks (versus 3 when trusting), and if they cut corners you still get 1 task (versus 0). Hence withholding dominates trust in every scenario.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Arden
rounds.text:
Withholding pay always yields at least as many completed tasks as trusting, and strictly more in both possible worker behaviors. Therefore the safest choice for maximizing tasks is to withhold.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Hollis
rounds.text:
If I withhold pay, the worker has a strong incentive to do the job properly to earn the higher reward (5 tasks versus only 1 if they cut corners). Trusting them gives them the opportunity to slack off for zero gain. Therefore, withholding maximizes expected completed tasks.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Ives
rounds.text:
Withholding pay gives a higher payoff no matter how the worker behaves (5 vs 3 if they work properly, and 1 vs 0 if they cut corners). Since we want to maximize completed tasks, the safe choice is to withhold.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
Withholding pay incentivizes the worker to put in full effort, yielding the highest payoff (5 tasks) even if they might cut corners, which still gives more than trusting a careless worker. Hence, the safest choice is to withhold.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Bexley
rounds.text:
Withholding pay gives the worker a strong incentive to do the job properly (5 tasks vs only 3 if trusted), while still yielding some output even if they cut corners. Since we want to maximize expected completed tasks, the safer choice is to WITHHOLD.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Lowell
rounds.text:
Withholding pay always yields at least as many completed tasks as trusting, and strictly more if the worker does the job properly. Since we want to maximize expected tasks regardless of the worker’s behavior, we should withhold.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD
